structured_payload.title: Ignition gateway restart and OptiSweep / WCS API response validation
structured_payload.summary: Use the Ignition gateway, Windows Event Viewer / services, and Apidog / WCS API surfaces to restart the Ignition gateway, verify the GetAgvStatuses response, and restart OptiSweep only if the API does not respond. The site operator must place and release the physical E-stop; support must not release it until the API response is confirmed.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use when the Ignition gateway or OptiSweep / WCS API is not responding and the site is held in the physical E-stop state pending recovery validation. Perform the Ignition gateway restart, verify the Ignition gateway, then validate OptiSweep through the GetAgvStatuses request before returning the system to operation.
not_for: Do not use to perform or release a physical E-stop remotely; only the site operator may perform those physical actions.
Do not release the physical E-stop before GetAgvStatuses returns a response after the documented validation and any required OptiSweep service restart.
Do not treat an HTTP 200 response as eliminating the recorded response-schema warning; the warning must be retained for review.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the Ignition gateway restart and the OptiSweep / WCS API validation using the Ignition gateway, Windows Event Viewer / services, and Apidog / WCS API surfaces.
The site operator places and releases the physical E-stop and confirms that auto bag-out can resume.
L2_support stops and escalates if the gateway, API, or OptiSweep service does not recover.
safety_notes: The site operator must place the system in the physical E-stop state before the restart sequence.
Keep the physical E-stop active during recovery.
Do not release the physical E-stop until the OptiSweep / WCS API response is confirmed.
Support must not perform or remotely release the physical E-stop.
access_or_tools_needed: Windows Event Viewer / services, including a Windows Administrator Command Prompt
Physical floor / grid for the site operator's E-stop and release

access_required: L2 support access to the Ignition gateway, Windows Event Viewer / services, and Apidog / WCS API.
A site operator available at the physical floor / grid to place and release the physical E-stop.
system_preconditions: The site is in the physical E-stop state before the restart sequence begins.
The physical E-stop remains active until API responsiveness is confirmed.

visual_references.description: Windows Administrator Command Prompt showing the Ignition directory, `gwcmd -r`, and `Waiting for Gateway restart...`.
Ignition gateway Status > Systems > Overview showing Current Response Time and Recent Slow Response Events.

Windows Event Viewer / services surface showing OptiSweep selected with status Running and the Restart the service control visible.

steps.title: Place the system in the physical E-stop state
steps.purpose: Hold the site in a safe stopped state while the Ignition gateway and OptiSweep / WCS API recovery checks are performed.
steps.instruction: On the physical floor / grid, have the site operator place the system in the physical E-stop state and keep it active throughout recovery.
steps.expected_result: The physical E-stop is active and remains active while the Ignition gateway and OptiSweep / WCS API are restarted or checked.
steps.healthy_condition: The site confirms that the physical E-stop is engaged before L2 support begins the restart sequence.
steps.failure_condition: The site cannot confirm that the physical E-stop is active or the E-stop state changes during recovery.

actions.label: Engage physical E-stop
actions.exact_action: Have the site operator place the system in the physical E-stop state.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop if the site cannot confirm the physical E-stop state.
Escalate any safety uncertainty; do not continue toward E-stop release.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The E-stop is to remain in place during the Ignition and OptiSweep verification sequence and is released only after confirmation.

steps.title: Restart the Ignition gateway
steps.purpose: Initiate the source-supported Ignition gateway restart before checking gateway and OptiSweep / WCS API responsiveness.
steps.instruction: On the Windows Event Viewer / services surface, open a Windows Administrator Command Prompt, navigate to the Inductive Automation Ignition installation directory, run `gwcmd -r`, and wait for the console to show `Waiting for Gateway restart...`.
steps.expected_result: The Windows Administrator Command Prompt shows `gwcmd -r` executed from the Ignition directory and displays `Waiting for Gateway restart...`.
steps.healthy_condition: The restart command is accepted and the console enters the gateway-restart waiting state.
steps.failure_condition: The command cannot be run from the Ignition directory or the console does not show the gateway-restart waiting message.

actions.label: Run Ignition gateway restart
actions.exact_action: From `C:\Program Files\Inductive Automation\Ignition`, run `gwcmd -r`.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop and escalate if the Ignition gateway restart command cannot be executed or the gateway does not return for later verification.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: The command prompt shows navigation to the Ignition directory, execution of `gwcmd -r`, and `Waiting for Gateway restart...`.

steps.title: Verify the Ignition gateway Systems Overview
steps.purpose: Confirm that the Ignition gateway is responding after the restart.
steps.instruction: On the Ignition gateway, open Status > Systems > Overview and check that the page responds, including Current Response Time and Recent Slow Response Events.
steps.expected_result: The Ignition gateway Systems Overview responds and displays a Current Response Time; the incident evidence showed 11 ms and `No events to display` under Recent Slow Response Events.
steps.healthy_condition: The Systems Overview page loads with a current response-time value and no recent slow response events displayed.
steps.failure_condition: The Systems Overview page does not load or does not provide a responding gateway status.

actions.label: Inspect Ignition Systems Overview
actions.exact_action: Open Status > Systems > Overview and check Current Response Time and Recent Slow Response Events.

stop_or_escalate_if: Escalate if the Ignition gateway does not return to the Systems Overview page.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Ignition Status > Systems > Overview showed Current Response Time of 11 ms and Recent Slow Response Events: No events to display.

steps.title: Validate OptiSweep / WCS API responsiveness
steps.purpose: Verify that OptiSweep is responding to an AGV status request before the physical E-stop is released.
steps.instruction: On the Apidog / WCS API surface, send the `GetAgvStatuses` request and inspect the response for HTTP Success / Status 200 and returned AGV records, including visible status values such as `NORMAL`.
steps.expected_result: The GetAgvStatuses request returns HTTP 200 with AGV records; the incident response showed visible `NORMAL` status values.
steps.healthy_condition: The API client displays a successful 200 response containing AGV status records.
steps.failure_condition: The request does not respond or does not return AGV records.

actions.label: Send GetAgvStatuses request
actions.exact_action: In Apidog, send the `GetAgvStatuses` request and check the returned status and AGV records.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop before releasing the physical E-stop if GetAgvStatuses does not return a response.
Record the response-schema warning `Response data differs from endpoint spec` and `$ should be object` for review even when HTTP 200 and AGV records are returned.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: GetAgvStatuses returned Success / Status 200 with AGV records and visible NORMAL values.
The response returned HTTP 200 but showed `Response data differs from endpoint spec` and `$ should be object`.

steps.title: Restart OptiSweep only if GetAgvStatuses does not respond
steps.purpose: Restore OptiSweep service responsiveness when the post-Ignition-restart API check receives no response.
steps.instruction: If GetAgvStatuses does not respond, open Windows Event Viewer / services, select OptiSweep, use the visible `Restart the service` control, then return to Apidog / WCS API and send GetAgvStatuses again.
steps.expected_result: After the documented OptiSweep service restart, GetAgvStatuses returns a response with AGV records; Windows Event Viewer / services shows OptiSweep in a Running state when inspected.
steps.healthy_condition: The API responds after the conditional service restart and OptiSweep is shown as Running in Windows Event Viewer / services.
steps.failure_condition: The API remains nonresponsive or OptiSweep is not shown as Running after the restart attempt.

actions.label: Restart OptiSweep service
actions.exact_action: In Windows Event Viewer / services, select OptiSweep and use the visible `Restart the service` control.

actions.label: Repeat API validation
actions.exact_action: Send `GetAgvStatuses` again in Apidog / WCS API after the service restart.

stop_or_escalate_if: Stop before releasing the physical E-stop if GetAgvStatuses remains nonresponsive after the documented OptiSweep restart and repeat check.
Escalate if OptiSweep does not show Running.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: If the Get Statuses request gives no response, restart OptiSweep and confirm with another request before releasing the E-stop.
Windows Event Viewer / services shows OptiSweep selected with status Running and the Restart the service control visible; the screenshot does not prove that a restart was performed.

steps.title: Release the physical E-stop and confirm auto bag-out
steps.purpose: Return the site to operation only after Ignition and OptiSweep / WCS API responsiveness has been confirmed.
steps.instruction: After the GetAgvStatuses response is confirmed, have the site operator release the physical E-stop on the physical floor / grid and confirm that the site can resume the auto bag-out operation.
steps.expected_result: The site operator releases the physical E-stop and confirms that auto bag-out can resume.
steps.healthy_condition: The physical E-stop is released by the site operator after API confirmation and the site resumes auto bag-out.
steps.failure_condition: The API response has not been confirmed, the E-stop cannot be safely released, or auto bag-out cannot resume.

actions.label: Release physical E-stop
actions.exact_action: Have the site operator release the physical E-stop after the API response is confirmed.

actions.label: Confirm auto bag-out
actions.exact_action: Confirm that the site can resume the auto bag-out operation.

stop_or_escalate_if: Do not release the physical E-stop until GetAgvStatuses responsiveness is confirmed.
Escalate if the site cannot resume auto bag-out after the operator releases the E-stop.

source_evidence.quote_or_summary: Once the OptiSweep response is confirmed, release the E-stop.
The site was finishing the bag-out process before the system could be un-E-stopped.

success_criteria: The Ignition gateway Systems Overview responds after the restart.

GetAgvStatuses does not return a response.
OptiSweep does not show Running after the documented restart attempt.
The API returns a response-schema warning: `Response data differs from endpoint spec` and `$ should be object`.
The physical E-stop cannot be safely released or the site cannot resume auto bag-out.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if the Ignition gateway does not return to the Systems Overview page.
Escalate if GetAgvStatuses remains nonresponsive after the documented OptiSweep restart and repeat check.

structured_payload.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
structured_payload.summary: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) live read-only database surface to inspect robotics-related AGV state records when the RMS / fleet status UI reports AGVs out of sync or the robotic system is stopped. Compare the populated SSMS State results with the live RMS / fleet status UI; the listed state values do not independently establish a fault.
structured_payload.when_to_use: Use the live WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) surface to inspect AGV state records when the RMS / fleet status UI reports AGVs out of sync or the robotic system is stopped.
not_for: Do not use this diagnostic to infer that a listed AGV State value is abnormal without corresponding live RMS / fleet status UI context or SME interpretation.
Do not use it to modify database records or perform recovery actions.
Do not use it as a substitute for physical E-stop or other site safety actions.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support performs the read-only inspection in WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) and compares the results with the live RMS / fleet status UI.

safety_notes: This procedure is supported as a read-only diagnostic; do not modify database values.
Do not treat the displayed AGV State values as proof of a fault by themselves.
Escalate if the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) connection or query execution fails, or if expected AGV results are unavailable.

structured_payload.user_facing_summary: Use this response pattern when operators report that robots or AGVs are stopped, nothing is moving, the small sort is not running, or the robotic system is not responding. Confirm the scope and observable system state, investigate service and application health, restore the named robotic service or gateway through an approved procedure, correct residual AGV synchronization issues, and validate API and operational recovery.
structured_payload.playbook_goal: Restore stable robotic and sort operation by distinguishing a site-wide control-system or service interruption from a localized AGV condition, then validating service responsiveness, AGV state, and resumed automated operation.

nodes.title: Confirm the observable scope of the stoppage
nodes.intent: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide or broad robotic stoppage with abnormal control-system presentation rather than an isolated robot issue.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the report represents a site-wide or broad robotic stoppage with abnormal control-system presentation rather than an isolated robot issue.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to ask the site which affected areas or workflows are stopped, whether multiple robots are stationary, and whether automated sorting or hospital tote removal is affected; also inspect the RMS/HMI overview for a normally populated versus mostly blank operational display and any readable system or AGV error indicators.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident began with reports that nothing was moving, the small sort was not running, and the robotic system was not responding; RMS screenshots showed an abnormal mostly blank presentation.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to ask the site which affected areas or workflows are stopped, whether multiple robots are stationary, and whether automated sorting or hospital tote removal is affected; also inspect the RMS/HMI overview for a normally populated versus mostly blank operational display and any readable system or AGV error indicators.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator or support user confirms through site interview and the RMS/HMI view whether multiple robots or areas are stopped, the small sort or hospital workflow is affected, and the RMS page is populated normally. Unhealthy signals are broad non-movement, robotic-system nonresponse, or a mostly blank RMS page with an apparent '.NET Control not created.' message. Healthy signals are localized impact with otherwise normal fleet presentation. Inconclusive signals are an unclear scope report, unreadable RMS display, or unavailable site confirmation.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: RMS screenshots show ACB System 1 - RMS with a mostly blank panel and an apparent '.NET Control not created.' message; page 5.
Case comments and Teams messages record site reports that nothing was moving, the robotic system was not responding, and hospital totes could not be removed; pages 2 and 25.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet contains a site-wide stoppage report and a blank RMS/system-status presentation.

healthy_indicators: Site reports only a localized issue.
RMS overview is populated and shows normal system presentation.
Other automated areas continue operating.
unhealthy_indicators: Multiple areas or robots are stopped.
Nothing is moving or the robotic system is not responding.
Small sort or hospital workflow is unavailable.
RMS main panel is mostly blank or shows the apparent '.NET Control not created.' message.
inconclusive_indicators: Only one robot is reported stopped.
The RMS image or error sections cannot be read.
The site cannot confirm whether the stoppage is broad or localized.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If the scope cannot be confirmed or the evidence is limited to an unreadable interface, leave this path for retriage rather than assuming a system-wide service fault.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Reports stated that 4-6 bots were not moving, hospital totes could not be removed, and nothing was moving.
RMS page was mostly blank and displayed an apparent '.NET Control not created.' message.

nodes.primary_action: Ask the site/operator which areas/workflows are stopped and whether the impact is broad (multiple robots/areas) vs localized; then check the RMS overview for whether it is normally populated vs mostly blank with readable indicators (including the reported “.NET Control not created.” message).
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation of which areas/workflows are stopped (broad vs localized).
Count/extent of stationary robots/areas reported.
Whether small sort / hospital tote removal workflow is affected.
RMS overview presentation: populated vs mostly blank; any readable error/system/AGV indicators (including whether the “.NET Control not created.” message is visible/readable).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Impact is localized with otherwise normal fleet presentation; site confirms only specific areas/workflows are affected and automated operation continues elsewhere.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Broad stoppage is confirmed: multiple areas/robots are stopped; nothing is moving/robotic system not responding; small sort and/or hospital workflow unavailable; RMS main panel mostly blank with the apparent “.NET Control not created.” message.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Scope is unclear (e.g., only one robot reported stopped) or RMS image/error sections cannot be read or site cannot confirm broad vs localized impact.

optional_corroboration.note: If the RMS page is blank/unreadable, treat that as an evidence-quality limitation and do not assume a specific root cause until backend/service evidence is checked.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use the site interview to confirm scope first; then use RMS overview readability to classify evidence quality (populated vs mostly blank). If the scope is not broad or evidence is limited/unreadable, branch to retriage rather than presuming a site-wide control/service fault.

nodes.goal: Determine whether Windows evidence indicates an OptiSweep service termination or clustered WCSWebApplication/application errors that correlate with the broad stoppage.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs for the named OptiSweep service and WCSWebApplication, including Service Control Manager termination events, the visible Event 7031 category, clustered application errors, and the WCSWebApplication Event 20102 failed-command evidence, while preserving timestamps and uncertainty.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source shows OptiSweep Event 7031 termination evidence and clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries around 6:35-6:36 AM.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs for the named OptiSweep service and WCSWebApplication, including Service Control Manager termination events, the visible Event 7031 category, clustered application errors, and the WCSWebApplication Event 20102 failed-command evidence, while preserving timestamps and uncertainty.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1, L2, or L3 support reviews Windows Event Viewer. Unhealthy signals are a System-log Service Control Manager event showing OptiSweep terminated unexpectedly, or Application-log WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries clustered around the reported interruption, including the visible Event ID 20102 failed database-command evidence. Healthy signals are no relevant service termination or clustered application errors. Inconclusive signals are unavailable logs, ambiguous timestamps, or errors without a credible temporal relationship to the stoppage.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Incident artifacts show Windows Event Viewer Application and System logs, including WCSWebApplication errors and OptiSweep Event 7031; pages 27-29.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: Event Viewer artifacts directly show Service Control Manager Event 7031 and clustered application errors.
The packet names OptiSweep and WCSWebApplication and documents their abnormal events.

ontology_gaps: The supplied ontology does not provide a specific Event Viewer event-to-service recovery mapping beyond the named capability.
healthy_indicators: No relevant OptiSweep termination event is present in the incident window.
No clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error entries are present.
The reviewed service and application evidence is temporally unrelated to the reported symptoms.
unhealthy_indicators: Service Control Manager Event 7031 states that OptiSweep terminated unexpectedly.
Application-log entries show clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error events around the stoppage.
WCSWebApplication Event 20102 shows a failed database command near the interruption.
inconclusive_indicators: Event logs are unavailable or incomplete.
The event timestamp cannot be aligned with the symptom report.
The event text is unreadable or only indicates a generic warning.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Event 7031 states that the OptiSweep service terminated unexpectedly and that Windows planned a restart.
WCSWebApplication Event 20102 shows a failed database command.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect Windows Event Viewer / Services evidence for OptiSweep termination and clustered WCSWebApplication/application errors that temporally correlate with the stoppage.

evidence_to_collect: System-log evidence around the incident window for Service Control Manager termination of OptiSweep (e.g., Event 7031).
Application-log evidence for clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries around the same time.
Any visible WCSWebApplication Event 20102 failed-command evidence (or equivalent).

nodes.healthy_interpretation: No relevant OptiSweep termination or clustered WCSWebApplication/application errors exist in the incident window; any reviewed service/app evidence is temporally unrelated to the reported stoppage.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: OptiSweep terminated unexpectedly (e.g., Event 7031) and/or there are clustered WCSWebApplication/application errors (including Event 20102 failed database-command evidence) temporally correlating with the stoppage.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Event logs unavailable/incomplete, timestamps ambiguous, or errors are too generic/unreadable to establish credible temporal correlation.

optional_corroboration.note: If the site is reporting blank/unresponsive RMS, corroborate with backend service/system status evidence from the WCS side as allowed by the procedure (do not use SQL as a substitute for missing Windows log evidence when logs are available).

ontology_evidence.text: Capability wcs_service_health: Confirm OptiSweep / WCS Windows service health and related host recovery signals.. When: Blank RMS, service crash, unplanned restart, need OptiSweep service + SQL Agent checks. Not for: Single AGV active error without service-down evidence.. Surfaces: event_viewer, rms_ui, wcs_sql, ignition_gateway, stunnel, site_interview. Support contract: {"diagnostic_surfaces": ["wcs_sql", "event_viewer", "ignition_gateway", "wcs_api"], "control_surfaces": ["windows_services",

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Determine whether the broad stoppage is caused by an OptiSweep service termination and/or WCSWebApplication/application fault cluster; only then proceed to the approved service/gateway recovery step.

nodes.title: Restore the affected OptiSweep or gateway service through an approved procedure
nodes.intent: Perform the source-supported recovery direction for the affected control service or gateway when the authorized support role confirms an abnormal service or gateway state.
nodes.goal: Perform the source-supported recovery direction for the affected control service or gateway when the authorized support role confirms an abnormal service or gateway state.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized recovery of the named OptiSweep service or Ignition gateway, including safety prerequisites, role limits, recovery completion criteria, and the distinction between a service reset, gateway restart, and unsupported configuration or database changes.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source records OptiSweep reset activity, an Ignition gateway restart attempt, automatic service restart behavior, and later evidence of the OptiSweep service in a Running state.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized recovery of the named OptiSweep service or Ignition gateway, including safety prerequisites, role limits, recovery completion criteria, and the distinction between a service reset, gateway restart, and unsupported configuration or database changes.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1, L2, or L3 support records that the approved recovery procedure for the affected OptiSweep service or Ignition gateway has completed or is still in progress. Progress is indicated by a returned service or gateway status and an available post-recovery validation surface. Failure is indicated by an unavailable service, repeated termination, or an incomplete gateway restart. Inconclusive status means the procedure outcome is not visible or cannot be confirmed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Event Viewer showed OptiSweep termination and an automatic restart action; page 29.
The packet documents Ignition gateway restart activity and an Ignition Systems Overview page; pages 15-16.
Windows Services showed OptiSweep and its Running state; page 19.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not establish whether OptiSweep reset or Ignition gateway restart was the sufficient recovery action.
The exact recovery command sequence is intentionally excluded from this playbook candidate.
healthy_indicators: Authorized recovery is reported complete.
OptiSweep is shown as Running after the recovery attempt.
Ignition Systems Overview is reachable after gateway recovery.
unhealthy_indicators: OptiSweep remains stopped or terminates again.
Ignition gateway remains unavailable or the restart does not complete.
The same service or application errors recur immediately.
inconclusive_indicators: A restart is shown as in progress without a completion result.
A service is shown as Running but no responsiveness check has been completed.
The recovery action is described only in chat without direct status evidence.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not proceed with unsupported configuration, database, or server changes. Stop if the authorized recovery procedure or its safety prerequisites are unavailable.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: After resetting OptiSweep, RMS was used to locate and correct out-of-sync AGVs.
Ignition gateway restart activity was shown as waiting for gateway restart.
OptiSweep was shown as Running in Windows Services.

nodes.primary_action: If authorized and confirmed abnormal, restore the affected OptiSweep service and/or Ignition gateway through the approved recovery procedure, then record the recovery completion status.
evidence_to_collect: Recovery completion status from approved procedure (service/gateway state).
OptiSweep service state after recovery attempt (Running vs Stopped).
Ignition Systems Overview reachability/response after gateway recovery (if available).
Any evidence that the same termination/restart errors recur immediately.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Approved recovery is completed; OptiSweep is Running and Ignition Systems Overview is reachable.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: OptiSweep remains stopped or terminates again; Ignition gateway remains unavailable or restart does not complete; same errors recur immediately.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Restart/recovery reported but cannot be confirmed with status evidence; service shown Running but responsiveness check not yet completed.

optional_corroboration.note: Do not proceed to residual AGV correction until the control path responsiveness validation in the next node is completed.

nodes.intent: Confirm that the recovered control path responds before attempting residual AGV correction or releasing the site to automated operation.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the recovered control path responds before attempting residual AGV correction or releasing the site to automated operation.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep responsiveness through the incident-evidenced GetAgvStatuses API endpoint, inspect returned AGV records without treating the client schema warning as a confirmed service failure, and corroborate with Ignition Systems Overview and Windows Services when those surfaces are available.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source defines GetAgvStatuses as a post-restart responsiveness check and shows HTTP 200 with returned AGV records, while also documenting Ignition and Windows Services checks.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep responsiveness through the incident-evidenced GetAgvStatuses API endpoint, inspect returned AGV records without treating the client schema warning as a confirmed service failure, and corroborate with Ignition Systems Overview and Windows Services when those surfaces are available.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1, L2, or L3 support checks the named OptiSweep/WCS API and, where applicable, the Ignition Systems Overview and Windows Services state. Healthy signals are a successful GetAgvStatuses response with returned AGV records, an available gateway status page, and a Running OptiSweep service. Unhealthy signals are no API response, unavailable gateway, or a stopped or repeatedly failing service. Inconclusive signals are HTTP success with unclear data validity, such as the observed schema warning, or a status page without confirmation of current service responsiveness.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Ignition Systems Overview showed a current response time and no recent slow response events; page 16.
Windows Services showed OptiSweep as Running; page 19.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet documents GetAgvStatuses returning HTTP 200 with AGV records.
The packet names OptiSweep and documents service-state checks.
The packet includes an Ignition Systems Overview response-time check.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not define whether the API schema warning is an endpoint defect, client specification issue, or incident condition.
healthy_indicators: GetAgvStatuses returns HTTP 200 with AGV records.
OptiSweep is shown as Running.
Ignition Systems Overview is reachable and reports current response with no recent slow response events.
unhealthy_indicators: GetAgvStatuses does not respond or returns no usable records.
OptiSweep is stopped or unavailable.
Ignition gateway status is unavailable or shows sustained abnormal responsiveness.
inconclusive_indicators: HTTP 200 is returned but the API client reports that response data differs from the endpoint specification.
Returned records are present but their operational status cannot be interpreted.
A gateway page is reachable but the current relationship to the recovered service is unknown.

evidence_to_collect: GetAgvStatuses response: success vs no response; verify usable AGV records are returned.

nodes.healthy_interpretation: GetAgvStatuses returns HTTP 200 with returned AGV records; OptiSweep is Running; Ignition Systems Overview reachable and no sustained abnormal responsiveness is observed.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: GetAgvStatuses does not respond or returns no usable records; OptiSweep stopped/unavailable; Ignition gateway unavailable or sustained abnormal responsiveness.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: HTTP success but data validity unclear (e.g., API schema warning unresolved); returned records exist but operational interpretation uncertain; gateway page reachable but relationship to recovered service is unknown.

optional_corroboration.note: If the API shows HTTP 200 but the schema warning persists, still corroborate with service/gateway status indicators rather than escalating solely on the schema warning.

nodes.generated_guidance: Only proceed to residual AGV synchronization checks when responsiveness is confirmed; otherwise stop/escalate through the handoff gate.

nodes.title: Determine whether residual AGV synchronization issues remain
nodes.intent: Identify whether individual AGVs remain out of sync after service responsiveness has returned.
nodes.goal: Identify whether individual AGVs remain out of sync after service responsiveness has returned.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or map view for out-of-sync AGVs and to corroborate relevant robot state through the read-only robotics database view in SQL Server Management Studio or the GetAgvStatuses response; the procedure must define how to distinguish residual synchronization problems from normal charging, queueing, or exchange states.
nodes.source_supported_description: After the OptiSweep reset, RMS was used to locate and correct AGVs that remained out of sync; a separate artifact shows read-only SSMS inspection of AGV states.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or map view for out-of-sync AGVs and to corroborate relevant robot state through the read-only robotics database view in SQL Server Management Studio or the GetAgvStatuses response; the procedure must define how to distinguish residual synchronization problems from normal charging, queueing, or exchange states.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The operator or support user reviews the RMS fleet or map view and, where available to authorized remote support, corroborates the AGV state through the incident-evidenced SSMS robotics view or API response. Unhealthy signals are AGVs still marked out of sync, inconsistent with the expected fleet state, or not participating normally after service recovery. Healthy signals are no residual out-of-sync AGVs and a coherent fleet view. Inconclusive signals are unreadable AGV state, ambiguous waiting or charging states, or an API response whose records cannot be interpreted.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: Case comments state that RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs; page 26.
A readable artifact visibly shows SQL Server Management Studio with robotics-related AGV state results; page 24.
The packet includes GetAgvStatuses response records and status values; page 17.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source describes locating individual out-of-sync AGVs and includes backend AGV state evidence.
The RMS interface includes AGV error sections and the incident evidence includes AGV status and error-related records.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not define the authoritative state value that means out of sync.
The SQL artifact does not provide a validated interpretation for each displayed queue, charging, exchange, or waiting state.
healthy_indicators: RMS shows the expected fleet without residual out-of-sync indicators.
Read-only state evidence is coherent with the expected operational state.
No residual AGV errors or mismatched roster states are identified.
unhealthy_indicators: One or more AGVs remain reported as out of sync.
RMS and the corroborating status evidence disagree about AGV membership or state.
AGV error or abnormal-state indicators remain after service recovery.
inconclusive_indicators: The RMS map or AGV error sections are unreadable.
The API returns records but their state meaning is unclear.
The SSMS results show waiting, charging, staging, or exchange states without a validated interpretation.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: RMS was used to locate AGVs that were out of sync and fix them individually.
SQL Server Management Studio visibly showed robotics-related AGV state results.

nodes.primary_action: Determine whether residual AGVs remain out of sync after control-service responsiveness has returned by reviewing RMS fleet/map state and corroborating AGV robot/state via backend read-only evidence.
evidence_to_collect: RMS fleet/map view for out-of-sync indicators and which AGVs are affected.
Backend corroboration of robot state and/or location/destination states for the indicated AGVs (read-only).
Whether residual active errors exist (only if needed to explain out-of-sync).
If AI/SQL state meaning is unclear, record as inconclusive rather than guessing state semantics.
nodes.healthy_interpretation: No residual out-of-sync AGVs; coherent fleet view; corroborating read-only backend state matches the expected operational condition.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: One or more AGVs remain out of sync after service recovery; RMS and corroborating backend state disagree about membership/state; residual abnormal error/roster state persists.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS map/AGV state unreadable; backend results exist but state meaning cannot be interpreted; API records cannot be reliably mapped to out-of-sync definition.

optional_corroboration.note: If out-of-sync is suspected but interpretation is uncertain, corroborate using active error evidence (agv_active_errors) before attempting correction.

linked_primary_procedure.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Inspect AGV/robot state from the WCS/Helix Robotics database (read-only) to corroborate RMS out-of-sync claims.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Directly aligned to node_5 requirement to corroborate RMS with read-only robotics/AGV state from SSMS; also incident_case preferred source available in node_5 candidates.
match_gaps: Node also requires a clear definition of what value means 'out of sync'; the ontology snippet provided does not specify the exact enumeration/flag semantics for 'out of sync' in this playbook step.

nodes.generated_guidance: Use RMS to identify candidates (affected AGVs), then confirm via SSMS read-only robotics state. Do not attempt correction until the out-of-sync issue is actually evidenced and interpretable as residual synchronization problems (vs normal charging/queue/exchange states).

nodes.title: Correct residual AGV synchronization state
nodes.intent: Use the authorized RMS recovery procedure to correct individually identified out-of-sync AGVs after the control service is responsive.
nodes.goal: Use the authorized RMS recovery procedure to correct individually identified out-of-sync AGVs after the control service is responsive.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized RMS handling of an individually identified out-of-sync AGV, including safety preconditions, role limits, identification of the affected asset, correction completion criteria, and boundaries for physical AGV recovery or unsupported state changes.
nodes.source_supported_description: The historical response used RMS to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs one by one after resetting OptiSweep.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized RMS handling of an individually identified out-of-sync AGV, including safety preconditions, role limits, identification of the affected asset, correction completion criteria, and boundaries for physical AGV recovery or unsupported state changes.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The authorized operator or support role records that the identified AGV synchronization corrections are complete. Progress is indicated by the affected AGV no longer appearing out of sync in the RMS or corroborating state view. Failure is indicated by an AGV remaining out of sync, becoming unavailable, or requiring an unsupported physical or configuration action. Inconclusive status means the correction result cannot be confirmed.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source states that RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs individually; page 26.

ontology_gaps: The source does not describe the exact RMS correction operation or define when physical AGV recovery is required.
healthy_indicators: Each identified AGV is no longer represented as out of sync.
The RMS fleet view is coherent after the authorized correction.
No new AGV error or safety condition is introduced.
unhealthy_indicators: An identified AGV remains out of sync after the approved correction.
The AGV cannot be safely or consistently represented in the RMS state.
Correction requires an operation outside the authorized role or source-supported procedure.
inconclusive_indicators: RMS state does not refresh or is unreadable.
The source state and displayed state cannot be correlated.
The correction appears complete but automated operation has not yet been validated.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Stop if the identified AGV requires physical handling, an E-stop decision, configuration change, database mutation, or another action not covered by the authorized procedure.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: After resetting OptiSweep, RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs individually.

nodes.primary_action: Use the authorized RMS recovery procedure to correct individually identified out-of-sync AGVs one by one, then confirm they no longer appear out of sync in RMS and corroborating state view.
evidence_to_collect: List of identified out-of-sync AGVs from node_5.
Completion evidence that each AGV correction is done and RMS state updates for each affected AGV.
Confirmation that corrected AGVs no longer appear out of sync (RMS refresh).
Any introduced new AGV error/safety condition (should not be introduced).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Each identified AGV is no longer represented as out of sync in RMS/corroborating state view; fleet view coherent and no new errors introduced.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: An identified AGV remains out of sync after authorized correction; AGV cannot be safely or consistently represented; correction requires action outside authorization/source-supported procedure.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS state does not refresh or cannot be correlated with the corrected asset; correction appears done but automated operation not yet validated.

optional_corroboration.note: If RMS does not refresh or state remains unclear after an authorized correction, do not continue with further corrective actions—route to escalation/hand-off.

linked_primary_procedure.title: Recover Empty AGVs That Lost Tasks After RMS Restart (Remove/Re-add AGVs Twice)
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Restore AGV state after RMS restart scenarios that cause lost tasks and residual out-of-sync behavior via authorized removal/re-add actions.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: This is the highest-scoring recovery candidate for the node_6 provided list, but the node intent is specifically 'authorized RMS handling of individually identified out-of-sync AGVs' without asserting the 'empty lost tasks after RMS restart' sub-pattern. Link is therefore low-confidence and likely needs SME adjustment to the exact out-of-sync sub-mechanism.
match_gaps: Node does not establish the out-of-sync cause as 'empty AGVs lost tasks after RMS restart'.
No node_6 candidate explicitly describes generic RMS correction of individually identified out-of-sync AGVs; several candidates are sub-specific (bump fault, empty AGVs, specific exchanges).

nodes.generated_guidance: Perform only the approved RMS correction action consistent with the identified out-of-sync mechanism from node_5 evidence. If the mechanism cannot be matched to a source-supported recovery procedure, stop and escalate with evidence rather than guessing a recovery action.

ontology_evidence.evidence: If active error/fault state contributes to residual out-of-sync, it should be evidenced before applying correction that depends on error classification.

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Apply the appropriate authorized RMS correction for residual out-of-sync AGVs, ensuring RMS state updates and no new faults are introduced.

linked_runbooks.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
linked_runbooks.purpose: Use the WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) live read-only database surface to inspect robotics-related AGV state records when the RMS / fleet status UI reports AGVs out of sync or the robotic system is stopped. Compare the populated SSMS State results with the live RMS / fleet status UI; the listed state values do not independently establish a fault.

nodes.trigger_condition: The authorized operator or support role records that the identified AGV synchronization corrections are complete. Progress is indicated by the affected AGV no longer appearing out of sync in the RMS or corroborating state view. Failure is indicated by an AGV remaining out of sync, becoming unavailable, or requiring an unsupported physical or configuration action. Inconclusive status means the correction result cannot be confirmed.

nodes.title: Validate stable automated operation
nodes.intent: Confirm that service responsiveness, AGV state, and the affected automated workflows have recovered sufficiently to declare the technical response successful.
nodes.goal: Confirm that service responsiveness, AGV state, and the affected automated workflows have recovered sufficiently to declare the technical response successful.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep service state, repeat the GetAgvStatuses responsiveness check, review RMS fleet state for residual synchronization issues, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement and the affected sort or bag-out workflow remain operational before declaring recovery.
nodes.source_supported_description: The historical response reported resumed auto bag-out after service reset and RMS correction, with API and service-state evidence used as validation.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep service state, repeat the GetAgvStatuses responsiveness check, review RMS fleet state for residual synchronization issues, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement and the affected sort or bag-out workflow remain operational before declaring recovery.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site operator confirms that automated movement and the affected sort workflow have resumed, while support confirms service/API responsiveness and no residual out-of-sync AGVs in the available status views. Healthy signals are resumed auto bag-out or automated operation, normal or coherent AGV status, and continued service responsiveness. Unhealthy signals are renewed non-movement, inability to complete the affected workflow, repeated service termination, or residual AGV synchronization issues. Inconclusive signals are only a service-running display, a single HTTP 200 response with unresolved data ambiguity, or recovery of one workflow without confirmation of broader operation.

source_used_surfaces.source_evidence: The source states that RMS was used to correct AGVs and that the site then resumed auto bag-out; page 26.
The source records GetAgvStatuses as the post-restart validation check and shows HTTP 200 with returned records; pages 17-18.
Windows Services showed OptiSweep in a Running state; page 19.
Case evidence states that the site resumed auto bag-out and was later reported as running; page 26 and close comment.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet documents site-wide stoppage and later resumed automated operation.
GetAgvStatuses was explicitly used as a post-restart validation check.
RMS was used to locate and correct out-of-sync AGVs.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not define a duration or monitoring interval for stable recovery.
The source confirms resumed auto bag-out but does not quantify whether every site function was restored.
healthy_indicators: GetAgvStatuses continues to return usable AGV records.
OptiSweep remains Running.
RMS shows no residual out-of-sync AGVs.
The site confirms automated movement and the affected sort or bag-out workflow have resumed.
unhealthy_indicators: Robots stop again or nothing is moving.
The affected sort or bag-out workflow remains unavailable.
OptiSweep terminates again or API responsiveness is lost.
Residual out-of-sync AGVs remain after correction.
inconclusive_indicators: Only the service Running state is confirmed.
The API returns HTTP 200 but the response schema warning remains unresolved.
The site reports one workflow resumed without confirming broader automated operation.
RMS status is unavailable or stale.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: If validation fails after the authorized recovery and AGV correction path, stop and prepare an evidence-based technical handoff rather than repeating unsupported recovery actions.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Instructions required confirming OptiSweep response with a Get Statuses request before releasing the E-stop.
After correcting out-of-sync AGVs, the site resumed the auto bag-out procedure.

nodes.primary_action: Validate that automated movement and the affected automated workflows (e.g., auto bag-out/small sort/hospital tote workflow) remain operational and stable after service responsiveness and residual AGV correction.
nodes.primary_surface: site_interview + wcs_api + rms_ui (plus event_viewer/SSMS corroboration when needed)
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation that automated movement has resumed and the affected workflow (sort/bag-out/tote removal) is functioning.
Re-check GetAgvStatuses (HTTP 200 with usable records) as the post-recovery API responsiveness check.
RMS fleet state shows no residual out-of-sync AGVs.
OptiSweep remains Running (Windows Services evidence if needed).
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Automated movement and affected workflow resume and remain stable; GetAgvStatuses continues to return usable records; RMS shows no residual out-of-sync AGVs; OptiSweep Running.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Robots stop again / nothing moving; affected workflow remains unavailable; OptiSweep terminates again or API responsiveness lost; residual out-of-sync AGVs remain after correction.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only service-running display confirmed; HTTP 200 returned but schema/record ambiguity remains; only one workflow resumed without confirming broader automation; RMS status unavailable/stale.

optional_corroboration.note: Do not declare recovery successful based on a single service screenshot or a single API response if RMS fleet state and site workflow confirmation are missing.

linked_primary_procedure.title: WCS / Helix DB (SSMS) AGV state inspection
linked_primary_procedure.purpose: Corroborate fleet/AGV state stability after recovery by inspecting robotics database read-only state.
linked_primary_procedure.rationale: Node_7 expects validation including GetAgvStatuses and site confirmation; the provided node_7 candidates include only SSMS AGV state inspection as a close corroboration procedure, not a direct 'post-recovery validation' API procedure.
match_gaps: Node_7 specifically requires repeating GetAgvStatuses responsiveness check and obtaining site workflow confirmation; SSMS inspection alone does not satisfy API responsiveness evidence and site operational confirmation.

nodes.generated_guidance: Collect both sides of the validation: operator confirmation that the workflow resumed/stays running, and support confirmation that service/API responsiveness and fleet coherence are still good. If any part fails or remains ambiguous, stop/escalate with evidence.

content.text: Use this troubleshooting flow when a site reports that robotic operation has stopped, AGVs are not moving or are out of sync, small sort activity has stopped, or the RMS view is blank or abnormal. Confirm the observable system state, inspect service and application evidence, recover the affected service or gateway through an authorized procedure, correct residual AGV state, and validate both service responsiveness and resumed operation.

structured_payload.title: Robotic system not responding with AGVs stopped or out of sync
structured_payload.user_facing_summary: Use this troubleshooting flow when a site reports that robotic operation has stopped, AGVs are not moving or are out of sync, small sort activity has stopped, or the RMS view is blank or abnormal. Confirm the observable system state, inspect service and application evidence, recover the affected service or gateway through an authorized procedure, correct residual AGV state, and validate both service responsiveness and resumed operation.
structured_payload.playbook_goal: Determine whether the site-wide stoppage is associated with an abnormal OptiSweep, WCSWebApplication, or related gateway state; support authorized recovery; identify residual AGV synchronization or state issues; and confirm stable robotic operation before release.
observed_entry_symptoms: Nothing is moving across the site or bots are stopped in multiple areas.
The robotic system is reported as not responding.
Small sort operation is not running.
AGVs are reported out of sync or several AGVs stop after a heartbeat issue.
Totes cannot be removed from the hospital workflow.
RMS or HMI is mostly blank or displays an apparent ".NET Control not created." message.
The site reports no obvious failed AGV even though automated movement has stopped.
support_user_language_examples: We can't get totes out of hospital
Several bots stopped after a heartbeat issue
Nothing is moving across the site or bots
The robotic system is reported as not responding
Small sort operation is not running
AGVs are reported out of sync or several
Totes cannot be removed from the hospital workflow
RMS or HMI is mostly blank or displays
The site reports no obvious failed AGV even
affected_systems_or_components: Windows Event Viewer / Service Control Manager
structured_payload.confidence_reason: The packet provides clear observable entry symptoms, named diagnostic surfaces, a source-supported service failure signal, a high-level recovery sequence, residual AGV correction, and multiple validation signals. Exact root cause and the significance of some memory and RMS messages remain uncertain.

nodes.title: Confirm the stoppage pattern and abnormal control-system presentation
nodes.intent: Determine whether the report represents a broad robotic-operation stoppage with an abnormal RMS or HMI presentation rather than an isolated AGV issue.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the report represents a broad robotic-operation stoppage with an abnormal RMS or HMI presentation rather than an isolated AGV issue.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected zone or workflow has broad loss of movement, whether small sort or hospital handling is also stopped, and whether RMS/HMI shows a populated normal status view or a blank/control-not-created presentation. Use generic affected-zone and reported-robot questioning rather than incident-specific identifiers.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports a site-wide or multi-area motion stoppage, no obvious failed AGV, stopped small sort, hospital tote-removal difficulty, and abnormal RMS/HMI presentation.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to confirm with the site whether the affected zone or workflow has broad loss of movement, whether small sort or hospital handling is also stopped, and whether RMS/HMI shows a populated normal status view or a blank/control-not-created presentation. Use generic affected-zone and reported-robot questioning rather than incident-specific identifiers.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The site or operator confirms whether the affected area has broad loss of movement, whether the small sort or hospital workflow is also affected, and whether RMS/HMI is blank or shows an abnormal control message. In RMS/HMI, a healthy or alternate pattern is normal populated system status with localized impact only; an unhealthy pattern is broad stopped operation with blank or abnormal system presentation; inconclusive means the scope, affected workflow, or displayed message cannot be confirmed.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet supports determining overall fleet or system-down versus running state from the site report and abnormal RMS overview.
The packet includes reports of stopped bots and visible RMS system/AGV error sections, although no readable specific error rows were extracted.

ontology_gaps: No supplied mapping establishes the operational meaning of the apparent ".NET Control not created." message.
healthy_indicators: Site reports movement continuing normally or impact limited to one asset.
RMS/HMI displays populated normal operational content.
Small sort and hospital workflow are operating normally.
unhealthy_indicators: Nothing is moving across multiple areas.
Small sort is stopped or totes cannot be removed from hospital.
RMS/HMI is mostly blank or displays the apparent control-not-created message.
inconclusive_indicators: Only one robot or one local area is affected.
The RMS message cannot be read or its operational meaning is uncertain.
The site cannot confirm whether the issue is still active.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Reports state that 4-6 bots were not moving, totes could not be removed from hospital, and the site reported nothing was moving.
RMS page appears mostly blank and shows '.NET Control not created.'
Work order states that the robotic system was not responding and the small sort was not running.

nodes.primary_action: Confirm with the site whether the stoppage is broad (multi-area/no movement) and whether RMS/HMI is blank or shows an abnormal control presentation, then determine whether small sort and hospital handling are also impacted.
evidence_to_collect: Site confirmation: broad loss of movement vs localized impact (which areas/workflows)
Whether small sort is stopped and whether hospital workflow (e.g., tote removal) is also impacted
RMS/HMI presentation: populated normal overview/status vs blank or abnormal message (e.g., '.NET Control not created.')
Whether the issue is currently active vs intermittent (at least 'still happening now' confirmation)
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Stoppage scope is localized/limited to a small subset of assets or areas, and RMS/HMI shows populated normal system status (localized impact only). Small sort/hospital handling appear normal (or at least not broadly stopped).
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Broad stoppage is confirmed across multiple areas, and RMS/HMI is blank or shows an abnormal control presentation consistent with system-level loss of service/control rendering; small sort and hospital handling are also stopped/blocked.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Only a single robot/area appears affected, the RMS/HMI message is unreadable or its operational meaning cannot be established, or the site cannot confirm whether the issue is currently active.
nodes.generated_guidance: Use generic affected-zone and workflow questions (small sort + hospital handling) to classify scope, rather than assuming the apparent RMS message ('.NET Control not created.') is the root cause. If the site cannot confirm scope, treat this as inconclusive and do not jump to service recovery steps.

Not for: Single-AGV active error deep dive without overall context.. Surfaces: rms_ui, aveva_hmi, event_viewer, wcs_sql, site_interview. Support contract: {}. Backend mappings: []. ontology_evidence.title: Capability — AGV active errors

When: Site reports AGV stopped, alarms, bump, path lost, or software showing robot faults; corroborate RMS overview vs WCS truth. Not for: Physical bump recovery steps (use agv_physical_recovery); Ignition OPC alone; tote NoRead.. Surfaces: rms_ui, wcs_sql, wcs_api, site_interview, apidog. nodes.intent: Use the available Windows log evidence to determine whether OptiSweep or WCSWebApplication entered an abnormal state near the onset of the operational stoppage.
nodes.goal: Use the available Windows log evidence to determine whether OptiSweep or WCSWebApplication entered an abnormal state near the onset of the operational stoppage.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs for OptiSweep Service Control Manager termination events and clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error entries, and to correlate their timing with the reported stoppage without inferring root cause from the event alone.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source contains Event Viewer evidence of OptiSweep termination, clustered WCSWebApplication errors, a failed database command, and a later OptiSweep Running state.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs for OptiSweep Service Control Manager termination events and clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error entries, and to correlate their timing with the reported stoppage without inferring root cause from the event alone.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes Windows Event Viewer System and Application logs. An unhealthy pattern is an OptiSweep Service Control Manager termination event or clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries near the stoppage; a healthy or alternate pattern is no corresponding service or application failure, prompting another investigation; inconclusive means logs are unavailable, timestamps cannot be correlated, or event details are incomplete.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet directly shows Windows Event Viewer and Windows Services evidence for OptiSweep termination and service state.
The packet reports OptiSweep service failure and WCSWebApplication errors, supporting service-health investigation without confirming a definitive cause.
The packet shows clustered WCSWebApplication errors and a failed database command in the Application log.

Application log shows clustered WCSWebApplication or Application Error entries near the reported stoppage.

inconclusive_indicators: Only a current Running state is available without historical timing.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect Windows Event Viewer (System + Application) to determine whether OptiSweep terminated unexpectedly (e.g., 7031) and whether clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries and database-command failures occurred near the stoppage onset; correlate timing without assuming root cause from events alone.
nodes.primary_surface: Windows Event Viewer + Windows Services state
evidence_to_collect: OptiSweep Service Control Manager termination/unexpected restart events (e.g., 7031) and timestamps
WCSWebApplication and Application Error cluster entries near incident onset and timestamps
WCSWebApplication Event 20102 (failed database command) presence and timestamps
Current OptiSweep service state (Running vs Stopped) from Services/related host evidence
Ability to correlate event timestamps with when the site observed the operational stoppage
nodes.healthy_interpretation: No relevant OptiSweep termination or clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error evidence is found near symptom onset, or OptiSweep is running without corresponding abnormal events.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: OptiSweep unexpectedly terminated (e.g., Event 7031) and/or clustered WCSWebApplication/Application Error entries are present near the stoppage onset; WCSWebApplication shows evidence such as failed database command events (e.g., 20102).
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Evidence is unavailable, event details are unreadable, only current 'Running' state is known without timing correlation, or the events cannot be correlated with the operational stoppage time.

optional_corroboration.note: If an event suggests system faults, corroborate with an authoritative SSMS SystemActiveError/System-level fault view rather than treating Event Viewer alone as proof of causation.

nodes.generated_guidance: Treat events as correlation indicators. If logs clearly align with the outage onset, proceed to gateway health check; if they do not correlate, continue with residual fleet-state investigation instead of jumping to recovery.

ontology_evidence.text: Model CellCodeDatabaseModel (robotics): Stores all cell codes in the map. node_interpretation_mapping.failure: OptiSweep termination or correlated WCSWebApplication/Application Error evidence is present near onset.
node_interpretation_mapping.inconclusive: Logs cannot be correlated or are unavailable/incomplete.

nodes.title: Check whether Ignition gateway health is abnormal or merely a related observation
nodes.intent: Determine whether the Ignition gateway shows a current responsiveness problem or whether the memory observation is only follow-up context.
nodes.goal: Determine whether the Ignition gateway shows a current responsiveness problem or whether the memory observation is only follow-up context.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to inspect the Ignition gateway Systems Overview for gateway responsiveness, current response behavior, recent slow-response events, and available CPU or memory trend evidence, while treating unlabeled trend changes as inconclusive unless correlated with a confirmed failure.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source includes requests to determine whether Ignition crashed, memory trend charts, an Ignition Systems Overview showing 11 ms response and no recent slow-response events, and a note that memory did not indicate it caused a crash.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the Ignition gateway Systems Overview for gateway responsiveness, current response behavior, recent slow-response events, and available CPU or memory trend evidence, while treating unlabeled trend changes as inconclusive unless correlated with a confirmed failure.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes the Ignition Systems Overview and available memory or CPU trend evidence. A healthy signal is a responding gateway with a current response time and no recent slow-response events; an unhealthy signal is an unavailable or nonresponsive gateway or a clearly abnormal resource trend correlated with the stoppage; inconclusive means the snapshot is stale, the trend lacks labels, or the gateway state cannot be verified.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet directly shows an Ignition gateway Systems Overview with response and slow-response indicators.

ontology_gaps: The supplied evidence does not identify the meaning of the memory chart reference line or provide a validated causal threshold.
healthy_indicators: Ignition Systems Overview responds and shows a current response time.
Recent Slow Response Events shows no events to display.
Memory trend is described as looking better and remains below the visible reference line.
unhealthy_indicators: Ignition gateway cannot be reached or does not respond.
Recent slow-response activity or other gateway health indicators are clearly abnormal.
A resource trend is visibly abnormal and temporally correlates with the operational failure.
inconclusive_indicators: A memory trend changes sharply without a labeled threshold or causal evidence.
The snapshot has no reliable timestamp or is not clearly from the affected gateway.
The gateway responds normally after the incident but historical state cannot be reconstructed.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: Support stated that the memory trend did not indicate that memory caused a crash and suggested checking CPU trend.
Ignition Systems Overview shows current response time 11 ms and no recent slow-response events.
Memory trend remains below a higher visible reference line without an obvious threshold crossing.

nodes.primary_action: Check the Ignition gateway Systems Overview to determine whether the gateway is currently responsive/healthy and whether resource/performance observations are correlated with the stoppage (treat unlabeled trend changes as inconclusive).
nodes.primary_surface: Ignition gateway Systems Overview + related gateway indicators
evidence_to_collect: Ignition gateway current responsiveness (ability to load Systems Overview and observed response time)
Whether Recent Slow Response Events shows events (and timestamps if available)
Any resource trend evidence (CPU/memory) and whether it is labeled with thresholds/timestamps that correlate with the stoppage
Correlation: is gateway abnormal state contemporaneous with operational stoppage evidence?
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Ignition gateway is responding with a current response time and there are no recent slow-response events.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Ignition gateway is unreachable/nonresponsive, or performance indicators show abnormal resource behavior temporally correlated with the operational failure.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Resource trends are present but unlabeled/uncertain, snapshot timing cannot be verified, or gateway responsiveness appears normal but correlation cannot be established.

optional_corroboration.note: If Ignition is unhealthy/unresponsive, corroborate the downstream state by checking WCS/OptiSweep responsiveness (API status) or host/service evidence before initiating recovery.

nodes.generated_guidance: The memory review is context only unless you can prove it corresponds to a confirmed gateway failure. Proceed to authorized recovery when the gateway is unavailable or shows a correlated abnormal state; otherwise still move forward based on the earlier service/application failure evidence as per branch hints.

nodes.source_supported_description: After the OptiSweep reset, the source says RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs one by one. The packet also includes RMS map and SSMS state evidence.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to inspect the RMS fleet or map view for residual out-of-sync, unavailable, unmapped, or abnormal-state AGVs after service recovery, using generic asset identification and state-correction criteria. The procedure should distinguish diagnosis from any authorized AGV correction action.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: The operator or support role observes the RMS fleet/map state and, when authorized, corroborates with the source-supported AGV state evidence. A healthy signal is a normal fleet view with expected AGV participation and no residual synchronization issue; an unhealthy signal is one or more AGVs remaining out of sync or in an abnormal state after recovery; inconclusive means the roster, map, or state cannot be reliably read.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source describes locating individual out-of-sync AGVs and includes RMS map and backend state evidence.
The packet contains AGV error sections and reports of stopped or out-of-sync AGVs, but no readable individual error codes.
Residual AGV state must be evaluated in the context of restored fleet operation.

healthy_indicators: RMS shows the expected fleet and no residual out-of-sync indicators.
AGV state and location presentation are consistent with restored operation.
No unresolved AGV error or mapping anomaly remains visible.
unhealthy_indicators: RMS identifies AGVs as out of sync or otherwise abnormal after service recovery.
AGV roster, location, or map state is inconsistent with expected operation.

inconclusive_indicators: RMS is unavailable or remains blank.

nodes.primary_action: Inspect RMS fleet/map state to identify any residual AGVs that remain out of sync, unmapped, or in abnormal states after service/gateway recovery; corroborate backend truth when possible and when evidence is required.
nodes.primary_surface: RMS fleet/map state (and SSMS corroboration for backend truth if required/available)
evidence_to_collect: RMS fleet/map view state after recovery (blank vs populated, fleet participation)
Whether any AGVs remain out of sync/unmapped/abnormal after the service reset

nodes.healthy_interpretation: RMS shows the expected fleet with no residual out-of-sync indicators; AGV state/location presentation is consistent with restored operation.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: RMS identifies AGVs as out of sync/abnormal after recovery; roster/map is inconsistent with expected operation; site still observes stopped assets.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS is unavailable/blank; displayed state cannot be interpreted operationally; only a single AGV snapshot is available without fleet-wide confirmation.

optional_corroboration.note: When investigating residual synchronization or fleet state, corroborate RMS display with SSMS read-only backend evidence for robot/location state consistency.

ontology_evidence.title: WCS model — RobotDatabaseModel

source_refs.note: PascalCase model inventory; live query screenshot on p.77 supplied the full column list and example values

ontology_evidence.text: Model RobotDatabaseModel (robotics): Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.. Fields: Name: Robot code / AGV identifier (e.g. 1555058).; State: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). Observed live values include SWaitingInzone, Removed, SWaitingForExchange, GoCharge, MovingToChargerEntranceQueue, MovingToTipperQueue.; ToteId: Tote currently

nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Determines residual AGV state abnormality after service recovery and selects the next step: correction vs proceed to validation.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Query Active AGV Errors From the WCS Database
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Retrieve current active AGV error records from the WCS database by logging into the WCS primary server, opening the WCS database, creating a new query tab, entering the documented SQL query against [Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics].[dbo].[SystemActiveErrorModel], executing it, and reviewing the returned results.

evidence_collection_procedures.title: Check Geek+ RMS overall page for system faults vs AGV system faults (and handle blank RMS due to firewall)
evidence_collection_procedures.purpose: Use the Geek+ RMS / fleet status web UI to confirm the overall page is reachable and that it correctly separates fault categories: “system faults” on the left and “AGV system faults” on the right. If the RMS page is blank, treat it as a reachability/firewall symptom. Use the left/right placement to interpret whether the issue is communication loss vs an AGV that was commanded to move but is not in progress.

catalog_gaps: Missing corroboration for `device_roster_state`: roster/mapping abnormality — check RMS map monitor / robot roster (optionally WCS robot-location models for L2).
Missing corroboration for `fleet_system_status`: fleet/system-down status — check Overall System RMS / AGV status (optionally WCS system-state models for L2).
Missing corroboration for `agv_active_errors`: AGV active errors — check RMS active AGV faults and/or WCS/SSMS SystemActiveErrorModel (L2).

linked_runbooks.purpose: Retrieve current active AGV error records from the WCS database by logging into the WCS primary server, opening the WCS database, creating a new query tab, entering the documented SQL query against [Helix2x_1Prod_Robotics].[dbo].[SystemActiveErrorModel], executing it, and reviewing the returned results.

If the RMS page is blank, treat it as a reachability/firewall symptom. Use the left/right placement to interpret whether the issue is communication loss vs an AGV that was commanded to move but is not in progress.

fields.name: IsToteEmpty
fields.meaning: Whether the tote currently on the robot is empty (1) or not (0)

fields.name: ToteId
fields.meaning: Tote currently associated with robot (labeled ToteId in the live query results

fields.name: Angle
fields.meaning: Robot heading/angle at its current location

fields.name: CellCode
fields.meaning: Current cell/lattice code the robot is reporting (cross-references CellCodeDatabaseModel.CellCode)

fields.name: ChargesSinceLastCharged
fields.meaning: Count of charge cycles since the robot was last fully charged

fields.name: LastCommandGuid
fields.meaning: GUID of the last command sent to this robot (cross-references RobotCommandDatabaseModel)

fields.name: State
fields.meaning: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). Observed live values include SWaitingInzone, Removed, SWaitingForExchange, GoCharge, MovingToChargerEntranceQueue, MovingToTipperQueue

node_interpretation_mapping.failure: Residual AGV state abnormality is indicated.
