nodes.title: Apply authorized correction for residual AGV synchronization or state issues
nodes.intent: Perform the approved correction for AGVs identified as out of sync or otherwise abnormal, without treating the historical correction as a universal procedure.
nodes.goal: Perform the approved correction for AGVs identified as out of sync or otherwise abnormal, without treating the historical correction as a universal procedure.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed for authorized RMS-based correction of an identified out-of-sync or abnormal AGV state, including safety prerequisites, asset-selection controls, role limits, and criteria for stopping before any physical AGV recovery. Exact historical correction steps are intentionally left to the procedure layer.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source reports that RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs after the OptiSweep reset, but it does not provide a complete reusable procedure.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed for authorized RMS-based correction of an identified out-of-sync or abnormal AGV state, including safety prerequisites, asset-selection controls, role limits, and criteria for stopping before any physical AGV recovery. Exact historical correction steps are intentionally left to the procedure layer.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: An authorized role records that the identified AGV state correction has completed. Progress is indicated by the affected AGV returning to an expected state and no longer blocking fleet operation; failure is indicated by persistent abnormal state or repeated loss of synchronization; inconclusive means the correction outcome cannot be observed.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The source supports correction of residual AGV state identified through RMS.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not specify the approved correction mechanism or distinguish software correction from physical recovery.
healthy_indicators: The affected AGV presents the expected state after authorized correction.
Fleet operation can proceed without the same synchronization anomaly recurring immediately.
unhealthy_indicators: The AGV remains out of sync or returns to an abnormal state.
Correction would require an unsupported or unsafe action.
Multiple assets remain affected beyond the supported correction scope.
inconclusive_indicators: RMS does not refresh or the resulting state cannot be observed.
The source-supported correction path does not identify the affected asset clearly.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Do not substitute physical AGV handling, E-stop, or configuration changes for this node. Stop if the approved RMS correction scope or safety preconditions are not clear.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: RMS was used to locate and fix out-of-sync AGVs after the service reset.

nodes.primary_action: Apply the approved RMS-based correction for the specific residual out-of-sync/abnormal AGV state identified in node_5, ensuring safety prerequisites and stopping if the scope is unclear or action would become unsafe/unsupported.
nodes.primary_surface: RMS fleet state (and any authorized RMS controls per procedure)
evidence_to_collect: Which AGV(s)/assets are corrected (identified generically by the RMS view as supported by procedure)
Evidence that the corrected AGV(s) return to expected state (RMS state refresh after correction)
Evidence that fleet operation is no longer blocked by the same synchronization anomaly
Stop criteria reached before any physical recovery if it would be out of scope/unsafe
nodes.healthy_interpretation: Affected AGVs present expected state after authorized correction; fleet operation can proceed without the same synchronization anomaly recurring immediately.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: AGVs remain out of sync/abnormal; correction would require unsupported/unsafe action; multiple assets remain affected beyond supported correction scope.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: RMS does not refresh or corrected state cannot be observed; corrected-path does not identify affected asset clearly.
nodes.generated_guidance: Do not substitute physical AGV handling here. If the approved RMS correction scope cannot be executed safely or cannot be confirmed, stop and proceed to escalation gate.

ontology_evidence.note: Residual out-of-sync state correction is governed by roster/map state; correction must be confirmed on the primary evidence surface (RMS) and should not expand into unsupported physical recovery.

nodes.title: Validate service responsiveness, AGV status, and resumed operation
nodes.intent: Confirm that the recovered service and fleet state support stable automated operation before declaring the troubleshooting path complete.
nodes.goal: Confirm that the recovered service and fleet state support stable automated operation before declaring the troubleshooting path complete.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep responsiveness in Windows Services and through the source-evidenced GetAgvStatuses API client, inspect returned AGV status records, confirm RMS shows the expected fleet state, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed. Treat an HTTP 200 response with a schema warning as partial evidence rather than complete recovery.
nodes.source_supported_description: The source provides Windows Services, GetAgvStatuses API, RMS follow-up, and site resumption evidence, while explicitly leaving the API schema warning and complete restoration scope uncertain.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to validate OptiSweep responsiveness in Windows Services and through the source-evidenced GetAgvStatuses API client, inspect returned AGV status records, confirm RMS shows the expected fleet state, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed. Treat an HTTP 200 response with a schema warning as partial evidence rather than complete recovery.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support observes the OptiSweep service state and the GetAgvStatuses API, while the site observes RMS and operational movement. Healthy recovery is supported by a responding OptiSweep service, a successful status response with returned AGV records, expected AGV status values, and site confirmation that automated operation or auto bag-out has resumed. Unhealthy recovery is continued no-response, repeated service failure, abnormal AGV state, or continued stoppage; inconclusive means HTTP success occurs but returned data cannot be interpreted, schema validation remains ambiguous, or site operation is not confirmed.

ontology_capabilities.relevant_evidence: The packet directly shows a GetAgvStatuses API request returning HTTP 200 and records.
The source supports validating resumed fleet operation and site running state.
Returned AGV records and RMS review are used to assess residual fleet state.

ontology_gaps: The packet does not provide a validated interpretation of the API schema warning or a complete API-to-RMS state reconciliation rule.
healthy_indicators: OptiSweep is shown as Running.
GetAgvStatuses returns HTTP 200 and AGV records.
Returned records include expected normal-status values.
RMS no longer shows unresolved out-of-sync AGVs.
Site confirms automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed and remains stable.
unhealthy_indicators: GetAgvStatuses does not respond or returns no usable records.
OptiSweep is stopped or terminates again.
RMS still shows out-of-sync or abnormal AGVs.
The site remains stopped or cannot resume automated operation.
inconclusive_indicators: HTTP 200 is returned but the response schema warning prevents reliable interpretation.
The service is Running but the screenshot timing relative to recovery is unknown.
RMS or site confirmation is unavailable.
Auto bag-out resumes but broader fleet stability is not confirmed.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: GetAgvStatuses returned HTTP 200 with AGV records, including visible NORMAL values, but the API client reported a schema warning.
Windows Services shows OptiSweep Running.
After RMS correction of out-of-sync AGVs, the site resumed auto bag-out.

nodes.primary_action: Validate service responsiveness and fleet status after recovery/correction: confirm OptiSweep/Windows service availability, confirm GetAgvStatuses API returns usable records, confirm RMS shows expected fleet state, and obtain site confirmation that automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed and is stable.
nodes.performed_by: operator + L1_support (API) + L2_support (services/SQL corroboration if needed)
nodes.primary_surface: Windows Services + WCS/OptiSweep API (GetAgvStatuses) + RMS UI + site confirmation
evidence_to_collect: OptiSweep service state in Windows Services (Running vs stopped) and any restart/termination indicators
GetAgvStatuses API: HTTP status, and whether returned records can be interpreted (handle schema warnings as partial evidence)
Returned AGV status values align with expected normal state (as defined by the API/RMS mapping used on site)
RMS no longer shows unresolved out-of-sync AGVs / abnormal fleet indications
Site confirmation: automated movement or auto bag-out has resumed and remains stable
nodes.healthy_interpretation: OptiSweep is Running; GetAgvStatuses returns HTTP 200 with interpretable AGV records including expected normal-status values; RMS shows no unresolved out-of-sync; site confirms resumed stable automated operation/auto bag-out.
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: GetAgvStatuses does not respond or returns no usable records; OptiSweep stops/terminates again; RMS still shows out-of-sync/abnormal AGVs; site cannot resume automated operation.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: HTTP 200 occurs but schema warning prevents reliable interpretation; service is Running but timing relative to recovery is unclear; RMS/site confirmation unavailable.
nodes.generated_guidance: Do not treat API reachability (HTTP 200) alone as complete recovery—especially when a schema warning is present. Stable operation must be confirmed by both evidence and site observation.

nodes.title: Stop and escalate when recovery or validation remains unsupported or fails
nodes.intent: Hand off only when the supported diagnostic, recovery, and validation path cannot safely continue or does not restore stable operation.
nodes.goal: Hand off only when the supported diagnostic, recovery, and validation path cannot safely continue or does not restore stable operation.
nodes.runbook_placeholder: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff with Event Viewer System and Application evidence, Windows Services state, Ignition gateway status, GetAgvStatuses response evidence, RMS fleet-state evidence, recovery actions attempted, validation results, safety constraints, and explicit stop criteria.
nodes.source_supported_description: The incident evidence supports stopping when service recovery, AGV correction, or validation does not establish stable operation. Historical coordination and case-management activity are not used as escalation triggers.
nodes.needed_runbook_capability: Procedure needed to prepare an escalation handoff with Event Viewer System and Application evidence, Windows Services state, Ignition gateway status, GetAgvStatuses response evidence, RMS fleet-state evidence, recovery actions attempted, validation results, safety constraints, and explicit stop criteria.
nodes.expected_or_observed_result: L1/L2 support identifies an unsafe, unauthorized, unsupported, repeated, or unresolved condition. A healthy outcome is not applicable because this node is a stop gate; an escalation condition is continued service failure, unavailable evidence, unresolved AGV state, failed validation, or a required action outside the current role; inconclusive means the evidence package is insufficient to determine whether recovery succeeded.
ontology_gaps: The packet does not define a canonical escalation evidence schema or role-specific handoff format.
unhealthy_indicators: The service or gateway cannot be recovered through an authorized supported procedure.
OptiSweep terminates again or API validation fails after recovery.
AGVs remain out of sync or automated operation does not resume.
Required action involves unsupported configuration, database mutation, physical recovery, or a role without access.
inconclusive_indicators: Evidence surfaces are unavailable or contradictory.
The API responds but the returned data cannot be interpreted.
Current service state is known but recovery timing and operational outcome are not.
nodes.stop_or_escalation_note: Escalate because the supported path is unsafe, unauthorized, unsupported, or unresolved after available diagnostics and validation—not merely because the historical incident involved collaboration or was unfamiliar.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: API returned HTTP 200 but showed a response-schema warning.
OptiSweep termination was recorded, but successful automatic restart was not confirmed.

nodes.primary_action: Stop the supported troubleshooting/recovery path and prepare an evidence-based escalation handoff package because recovery/validation remains unsupported, fails, or remains unresolved/ambiguous.
nodes.performed_by: L2_support (with L1_support evidence gathering as needed)
nodes.primary_surface: Evidence surfaces: Event Viewer, Windows Services, Ignition gateway, GetAgvStatuses (WCS API), RMS UI, and site confirmation
evidence_to_collect: Event Viewer System/Application evidence (OptiSweep and WCSWebApplication failures and/or lack of resolution)
Windows Services state (current and/or post-recovery)
Ignition gateway status (reachable/responding vs not)
GetAgvStatuses response evidence (HTTP results and schema warning if present)
RMS fleet-state evidence (whether out-of-sync indicators persist)
Recovery actions attempted and their outcomes (what succeeded/failed)
Validation results and explicit stop criteria and safety constraints
nodes.unhealthy_interpretation: Escalation is required: recovery/validation cannot be completed safely through supported procedures, recovery fails/repeats, AGV state remains unresolved, API validation fails after recovery, or evidence package remains contradictory/uninterpretable.
nodes.inconclusive_interpretation: Evidence package is insufficient or contradictory such that whether recovery succeeded cannot be determined.

optional_corroboration.note: If the failure is tied to recurring service restarts/crashes, include full timing evidence from Event Viewer to support a product defect/RCA escalation.

nodes.generated_guidance: Escalate based on unsafe/unsupported/unresolved conditions—not merely because the historical incident involved collaboration. Package enough evidence to allow the next team to determine whether a deeper recovery, product defect escalation, or additional technical ownership is required.
nodes.diagnostic_interpretation: Stop gate: routes away from supported path into escalation.
